title: Bitly
prompt: Design a URL shortener like Bitly. Users paste a long URL and receive a short URL; visiting the short URL redirects to the original. Target ~100M daily active users and ~1B URLs over the lifetime of the service.

stages.title: Functional Requirements
stages.questionPrompt: What are the core functional requirements for this system?
stages.howToAnswer: List 3-5 'Users should be able to...' statements covering the must-have behavior. Skip nice-to-haves like analytics or custom domains unless explicitly asked.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Twitter):
bullets: Users see a feed of tweets from people they follow

must: Users can submit a long URL and receive a short URL
Visiting the short URL redirects to the long URL
avoid: Drifting into analytics, dashboards, or accounts unless asked
Vague phrasing without explicit user actions

stages.sampleAnswer:
1. Users should be able to submit a long URL and receive a shortened URL.
2. Users should be able to specify an optional custom alias and/or expiration.
3. Users should be able to access the original URL by visiting the shortened URL.

stages.title: Non-Functional Requirements
stages.questionPrompt: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?
stages.howToAnswer: Cover availability vs consistency, latency targets with concrete numbers, scale (DAU/QPS/storage), and any uniqueness/durability constraints. Tie each requirement to a real product concern.

must: Low redirect latency with a concrete target (e.g., <100ms p99)

stages.sampleAnswer:
- Short URLs must be unique.
- Redirect latency: <100ms p99.
- Availability > consistency: a brief read-after-write delay is acceptable.
- Scale: ~1B URLs lifetime, ~100M DAU, read:write ~100:1.
- Durability: a URL mapping must not be lost once written.

stages.title: Core Entities
stages.questionPrompt: What are the core entities of this system?
stages.howToAnswer: List the nouns. Don't define schemas yet — that comes in High-Level Design.

should: Click event (if analytics are in scope)
avoid: Inventing entities the requirements don't justify

stages.sampleAnswer:
- URLMapping: shortCode → longURL, with optional expiration.
- (Optional) User: owns mappings if accounts are in scope.

stages.title: API
stages.howToAnswer: One endpoint per functional requirement. REST is the default — show method, path, request body shape, and response.

must: POST endpoint to create a short URL
GET endpoint that redirects from short URL to long URL
Returns the short URL on creation
should: Returns 301/302 with proper Location header on redirect
avoid: Putting URL details in URL path instead of body for create

stages.title: High-Level Design
stages.questionPrompt: Sketch the high-level architecture. Walk through each endpoint.
stages.howToAnswer: Boxes and arrows: client → load balancer → API service → database. Note schema fields next to the database. Walk through both endpoints end-to-end.

must: Client / Load balancer / API service / Database
Strategy for generating unique short codes (counter, hash, or random)
should: CDN consideration for the redirect path
Schema fields on the database (shortCode PK, longUrl, createdAt, expiresAt)
avoid: Skipping how short codes are generated

stages.sampleAnswer:
Client → ALB → URL Service (stateless) → Cache (Redis) → DB (key-value, e.g. DynamoDB)

Short code generation: 7-char base62 derived from a centrally-issued counter (e.g., a Redis INCR or a sharded counter service). Avoids collisions by construction.

Write path: API validates URL, allocates next counter, encodes to base62, writes mapping to DB, returns short URL.

Read path: short code → cache (hit: return). Cache miss → DB → populate cache → 302 redirect.

stages.title: Deep Dives
stages.questionPrompt: Harden the design against the non-functional requirements.
stages.howToAnswer: Pick 2-3 of: scaling reads, hot keys, ID-generation bottlenecks, abuse/spam, expiration, geo-distribution. Address each with a concrete mechanism.

must: Avoiding ID-generation bottleneck (sharded counter or pre-allocation batches)
should: Handling expired URLs (TTL job or lazy deletion)
Abuse prevention (rate limit on POST, URL reputation check)
avoid: Adding components without a justifying NFR

stages.sampleAnswer:
Reads (~100:1): Redis cache in front of DB; CloudFront in front of Redis for the most popular short codes.

ID generation: a counter service hands out ranges of 1000 IDs per API instance, instances encode locally with base62. Eliminates per-write coordination.

Expiration: lazy — on read, check expiresAt; if expired, return 410 and async-delete. Daily compaction job removes long-expired rows.

Abuse: per-IP rate limit on POST + Google Safe Browsing check on the long URL before storing.
